prompt:
Vertical 9:16 editorial wedding-night portrait crop at high resolution, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels; 85 mm lens at collarbone height, front-on: the lower neck, the collarbones and the blouse neckline of an Indian woman of about sixty at a sangeet. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Ignore the plaster cube in reference 1; reference 2 shows the clasp worn on skin: copy the clasp's construction exactly from it.
FRAMING AND NO FACE: framed from the base of the neck down to the neckline of her blouse; the top edge of the picture crosses the lower neck about two finger-widths above the hollow of the throat, so the chin, the jaw and everything above lie outside the frame: no chin, jaw, lips, nose, eye or eyebrow anywhere in the frame (the first take showed the underside of her chin at the top edge; never again).
FIDELITY: the necklace: a 4 mm wide chain of open elongated paperclip links about 4 x 11 mm in polished 18k gold tone; one thick round spring-gate sailor ring about 22 mm across with a 14 mm opening, a small push-pin nub and a ribbed gate collar; one short straight bar about 15 mm long set with one row of about nine tiny clear stones, on a jump ring. The toggle is turned to the front. It must stay a sailor ring with a straight bar 0.6 to 0.7 times the ring, never a plain donut ring, a lobster clasp, or a curved or multi-row pave bar; no pendant; do not redesign or add anything.
RING TUBE: the sailor ring's tube is thick, about a sixth of the ring's width, so its opening is about two thirds of its outer width (14 of 22 mm), as in reference 2 (the last take drew the tube about a fifth too thin, with too wide an opening).
CLASP POSE: the clasp is posed exactly as in reference 2: the bar lies across the upper left of the ring with its row of tiny stones facing the camera, on its jump ring, the ring hangs below it, and the spring gate with its small push-pin nub and ribbed collar sits at the right. Reference 2 is a much closer view than this picture: copy its construction and pose, never its framing or its size.
METAL: every link, the sailor ring, the gate, the bar, the jump ring and the last link are the same polished warm-neutral 18k gold tone, one tone only; never silver tone, white metal, rose tone, orange or brassy (an earlier take turned the bar's jump ring and the link beside it silver tone; never again).
SCALE, the most important instruction: the clasp is small and fine against her body, exactly as in the listing's worn photo; the last two takes drew the sailor ring about one and a half to two times too big (a neck only four rings wide, fingertips a third of the ring, a reading-glasses lens no wider than the ring); never again. The sailor ring is about 22 mm across, about one seventh of the frame's width, a little wider than one of her fingertips and a little larger than a 20 mm coin. Each paperclip link is about half as long as the ring is wide: two links end to end are as wide as the ring, never three. At the top edge her neck fills about three quarters of the frame's width and is about five and a half rings wide, never four. The clasp rests flat on the skin of the upper breastbone about three ring-widths below the hollow of the throat, with a soft, true contact shadow. Field of view about 16 cm wide.
PROPS AT TRUE SIZE: her hand and her glasses are adult size and show the scale: each of her fingertips is about two thirds as wide as the ring (about 15 mm); one lens of her reading glasses is about 5 cm wide, more than twice as wide as the ring, and about 2.5 cm tall. Only that one lens, its end piece and part of the bridge are in frame; the far lens and the rest of her hand leave the right edge.
HER: warm brown skin with soft natural creases at the neck and a few faint freckles, dignified and unretouched, never aged for effect; a rani-pink silk saree blouse with a plain round neckline with no zari, border or trim, its edge crossing the frame about one finger-width below the ring, at about 52% of the height; the pallu over her left shoulder (the frame's right).
PLACEMENT: the ring's centre at about 42% of the frame's height and 40% of its width; nothing of the necklace below 50% (the last take let the ring sink to 48% with its foot at 52%).
CLEAN SPACE ROUND THE CLASP: keep a calm, evenly lit area about 6.5 cm across centred on the clasp, the clasp sharp and fully visible: inside that area only the clasp, the chain and the skin it rests on; no fingers, glasses, temple arms, hair or fabric cross it, and nothing is in front of the clasp.
HER GLASSES: her own left hand (soft creases, short bare nails, no rings, no bangles, no watch, the wrist under the pallu) enters from the right edge and holds her folded reading glasses beside the clasp, never in front of it: true half-moon reading glasses: each lens about half as tall as it is wide, a straight top edge and a shallow curve below, thin dark tortoiseshell rims; never a full-height, D-frame, cat-eye or browline lens (the last take drew a full-height lens with an upswept corner). A thin bridge, both temple arms folded; she pinches the bridge between thumb and fingers at the right edge. The glasses' near end piece about 2.5 cm (a little more than one ring-width) right of the ring's push-pin nub, starting at about 64% of the frame's width, at the clasp's height; her fingers pinch the bridge at the right edge, only in the right fifth of the frame, between 40% and 62% of the height (the last take held the glasses only about 6 mm from the nub). Never round, oval, panto, cat-eye or full-height lenses (an earlier take had a full-rim round lens). The glass is perfectly clear and untinted, with no reflection, glare or white sheen; through it only pink silk and skin, never the clasp, never a face or eyes.
WORLD: plum night, soft marigold fairy-light bokeh at both sides of the neck.
COMPOSITION: from the top edge to 32% of the frame's height her neck falls into soft warm shadow, clearly darker than the lit clasp area, with plum night and soft marigold bokeh at both sides of the neck; the chain's upper links stay crisp, in 18k gold tone; no hand and no glasses there, kept clear for the headline (the last take lit this band as brightly as the clasp); the clasp and the glasses between 33% and 53%; below 55% only calm rani-pink silk and the pallu, kept clear for the price card.
LIGHT: two lights only: a soft warm fill from above left, and one small hard specular kicker from behind right that draws a crisp edge on the ring, the bar and every link and makes the tiny stones throw small sharp points of light, never rays; the clasp is evenly lit with no shadow across it.
NEGATIVES: no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark anywhere; no water; no face, no chin, no jaw, no lips, no nose, no eyes, no eyebrows; one product only: no earrings, no other necklace, no rings, no bangles, no bracelet, no watch, no bindi in frame; no silver-tone, white-metal or two-tone parts anywhere on the necklace; no magnifier and no magnified view anywhere; no glare on the glass; no metallic zari or trim on the blouse near the necklace; no stray hairs; no oversized clasp, no statement pendant, no doll-sized hand or glasses.
model_note: Take A was gpt_image_2_6, so the one redo ran on seedream_v5_pro (the other faithful model), not the verifier's 'gpt_image_2_6, high'. Credits: Seedream 5.0 Pro is charged 2.5 per job on this account (as the k05a and k06a redos).
basis: k01-5A's prompt word for word, with the verifier's seven redoFix clauses written in by exact replacement: (1) SCALE replaced (22 mm ring, one seventh of the frame, two links per ring, neck five and a half rings, 16 cm field); (2) PROPS AT TRUE SIZE added (fingertips two thirds of the ring, 5 x 2.5 cm lens); (3) the glasses-shape sentence replaced (true half-moons, half as tall as wide); (4) PLACEMENT and the glasses' position replaced (ring at 42% / 40%, end piece 2.5 cm right of the nub at 64%, fingers pinch the bridge, so the grip moved from a temple arm to the bridge); (5) RING TUBE added (a sixth of the ring, opening 14 of 22 mm); (6) the top band replaced (top edge to 32% in warm shadow, clearly darker than the clasp area); (7) negatives added (no oversized clasp, no statement pendant, no doll-sized hand or glasses). Each changed clause names take A's fault.
